correctness.rationale: The Lagrange polynomial basis yields a nilpotent second-differentiation matrix, so the local exponential center rows are finite exact polynomials in the diffusion ratio. Complete sign factoring gives five-node positivity {0} union [1/6,2/3], and seven-node positivity {0} union [(5-sqrt(10))/10,(5+sqrt(10))/10]. Five-node Fourier conditions follow from the explicit quadratic symbol. Seven-node symbol is strictly decreasing in t=sin^2(theta/2) because its derivative equals -4mu/15 times a sum of a square and a polynomial bounded below by 3. The Nyquist cubic derivative equals 1440(mu-5/12)^2+22, ensuring a unique positive root. A negative second-neighbor first coefficient and negative large-mu near-outer coefficient prove the all-stencil obstructions. value.rationale: The target is a recently introduced sparse local matrix-exponential integrator whose claimed high-CFL behavior motivates sharp discrete guarantees. The finding locates exact positive-state step intervals rather than generic negative-coefficient examples, and establishes that decreasing a timestep can destroy positivity before it recovers at intermediate scale. The seven-point spectral endpoint exceeds its positivity endpoint by a positive explicit amount, yielding a quantified safe-step design distinction. The universal short- and long-step obstructions show this is a structural issue of all higher centered interpolatory heat exponentials. Exact finite classifications of natural consecutive stencil widths are useful numerical reference cases without a downstream runtime theorem.
